tax.text: Brown supports higher taxes on wealthy people and corporations and removing the FICA income cap to strengthen Social Security.
tax.quote: People who make more should pay more in taxes. It's not only the tax rates that need to be changed, it's the loopholes that need to be eliminated. The problem is that fat cats use corporations to avoid taxes and accountability. Corporations must be taxed by wealth not income because they are by design meant to report very little income. Removing the cap on FICA income would make social security solvent immediately.

wages.text: Brown called for a living wage and a 32-hour workweek alongside other family supports.
wages.quote: A living wage, maternity leave, affordable healthcare, good education, affordable housing, and a 32-hour work week would be better things to do if they really cared about kids.

immigration.text: Brown supports sanctuary cities and protections against human-rights violations during immigration enforcement.
immigration.quote: People have a right and responsibility to protect anyone whose human rights are being violated. Sanctuary cities are a reaction to human rights violations.

guns.text: Brown said the Second Amendment should be expanded to give people more power over government.
guns.quote: A true liberal would expand the second amendment giving people more power over the Government.

abortion.text: Brown says abortion is a personal decision that government should not control.
abortion.quote: People need to be allowed to make all personal decisions and be guided by their inner voice. We need to let God be the judge whenever possible. What is right for one may not be right for another. Abortion is a personal issue that must be made by individuals.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Brown opposes allowing transgender women to compete in women's sports.
gender.quote: The reason people worked hard to pass title 9 is because men and women have different abilities. If we allow trans athletes to compete against women, we defeat the entire purpose of title 9.

cannabis.text: Brown opposes drug prohibition and describes control over drug use as a matter of personal autonomy.
cannabis.quote: A country that bans drugs is banning the right to control your own consciousness.

health.text: Brown supports making government-funded health insurance available to everyone while retaining private options.
health.quote: B. People should not be punished for being sick. It is a crime against humanity that more people are bankrupted by medical problems than for any other reason.

energy.text: Brown says energy production and use must change and makes protecting the planet government's highest priority.
energy.quote: It is necessary to change the way we use and produce energy. We are not separate from the planet and if we destroy our home we will be left with nothing. Protecting the planet is job # 1 for every government on earth and survival depends on it.

voting.text: Brown supports requiring photo identification and a national identification system for voting.
voting.quote: If photo ID is required to drink or drive it makes no sense that photo ID is not required to vote. If Citizen's can have rights that non-citizens can't have a national ID is necessary.

tax.text: Romero criticized H.R. 1's tax cuts as masking cuts to health care and food assistance and said he would reverse the law.
tax.quote: Romero regularly criticized Hurd’s vote for the legislation, which is also known as H.R. 1, for cuts that it would make to healthcare and food assistance, describing the middle-class tax cut portion of the legislation as “sugar” to cover up less popular parts of the legislation.

wages.text: Romero supports raising the federal minimum wage to between $12 and $15 per hour.
wages.quote: Sí, dijo Romero, a entre 12 y 15 dólares por hora.

trade.text: Romero says he would repeal the Trump administration's tariffs.
trade.quote: I’m going to fight to make it easier, starting with repealing these disastrous tariffs and expanding the Family Tax Credits.

debt.text: Romero opposes cuts to Medicare and says he would keep rural hospitals funded.
debt.quote: The One Big Ugly Bill completely turned our health care network on its head — Medicare, Medicaid, & SNAP were decimated and people were kicked off their health plans.

housing.text: Romero supports building more housing and removing regulatory barriers to construction.
housing.quote: We need to build more housing and bring down the cost of staying here.

immigration.text: Romero supports a citizenship path for long-term law-abiding residents, more immigration judges, and protections for people seeking refuge.
immigration.quote: Part of immigration reform needs to include a path to citizenship for long-term, law-abiding community members, and provide for more immigration judges to detain the bad guys and protect those seeking safe haven.

abortion.text: Romero says he would protect access to reproductive health care.
abortion.quote: We’ve got to keep rural hospitals open and funded, allow medicare to negotiate lower drug prices, and protect women’s access to reproductive healthcare.

health.text: Romero supports funding rural hospitals and allowing Medicare to negotiate prescription-drug prices.
health.quote: We’ve got to keep rural hospitals open and funded, allow medicare to negotiate lower drug prices, and protect women’s access to reproductive healthcare.

energy.text: Romero favors an all-of-the-above strategy centered on reliable, affordable energy while also developing alternatives.
energy.quote: An all-of-the-above approach is the only way we provide the reliable and affordable energy our communities need and deserve.

tax.text: Hurd voted for the 2025 reconciliation law, citing extensions of tax cuts as a benefit and estimating that four percent of his district’s Medicaid recipients might lose coverage.
tax.quote: no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, an extension of the tax cuts from 2017, a child tax credit increase, those help working families and middle class families that predominate in the 3rd Congressional District

wages.text: Asked about raising the minimum wage, Hurd said he was inclined to leave the decision to the market.
wages.quote: inclined to let the market make that decision.

trade.text: Hurd opposes sweeping tariffs because of consumer costs but supports targeted tariffs against unfair trade practices.
trade.quote: Instead of broadly raising tariffs, I support targeted trade policies that address specific unfair practices while strengthening our domestic economy by reducing regulations, lowering taxes, and encouraging innovation.

housing.text: Hurd supports expanding housing supply, streamlining zoning and regulations, and encouraging modular and manufactured housing.
housing.quote: As a member of Congress, I would support these state and local decision-makers while working to support policies that expand housing supply, reduce regulatory costs, and encourage innovative solutions to increase attainability.

schools.text: Hurd supports public funding for private, charter, and religious-school choices.
schools.quote: I support school choice funding for private schools, including private charter schools and religious schools. I believe that parents should have the ability to choose the best educational options for their children.

safety.text: Hurd requested $179,000 for computers, protective equipment, and investigative support for the Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office.
safety.quote: Funding would be used to purchase computer monitors, computer towers, vest carriers, and new plates for the office.

immigration.text: Hurd calls for immediate border enforcement while also supporting expanded legal immigration and worker pathways.
immigration.quote: Our country has always been a nation of immigrants. Jeff strongly supports legal immigration and expanding opportunities for legal immigrants. But a country that can’t control its border isn’t meeting its fundamental responsibilities toward its citizens—including national security, economic security, and upholding the rule of law.

guns.text: Hurd emphasizes gun-owner rights but says red-flag laws can be effective when accompanied by due-process protections.
guns.quote: As a gun owner and a firm believer in the Second Amendment, I am committed to finding solutions to prevent gun violence and school shootings. However, any measures we take must respect the constitutional rights of law-abiding citizens. Red Flag Laws and Extreme Risk Protection Orders can be effective tools if implemented with due process protections.

abortion.text: Hurd identifies as pro-life and supports some exceptions, while opposing a national abortion ban and leaving most policy to states.
abortion.quote: And what I tell my pro-choice friends that are unhappy with me because I'm pro-life, but I also have a bunch of pro-life friends who are unhappy with me because I believe in exceptions and because I also believe this is an issue that should be primarily left to the states.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Hurd voted for the House bill requiring federally funded school athletics to determine sex from reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

energy.text: Hurd supports expanded production of oil, natural gas, coal, nuclear power, and competitively priced renewable energy to lower costs and protect jobs.
energy.quote: Jeff supports the responsible development of all Colorado energy resources. This includes some of the cleanest oil and natural gas molecules in the world.

voting.text: Hurd supports proof-of-citizenship requirements for federal voter registration and more voter-roll checks.
voting.quote: Hurd said he supports federal legislation requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, arguing it would strengthen confidence in election integrity.
